nodes.ask: Possible overdose or poisoning. First moves?
options: ABCs, fingerstick glucose, ECG, and the poison center
A urine drug screen first, to name the drug before treating
Activated charcoal first, ahead of the ECG and the glucose
Flumazenil and naloxone together, to wake the patient for a history
nodes.chainStep: Airway, breathing, circulation; fingerstick glucose; 12-lead ECG for QRS and QTc; IV access and a metabolic panel; call the poison center (1-800-222-1222)
nodes.why: Stabilize first: airway, breathing and circulation, with intubation when coma leaves the airway unprotected. A glucose finds hypoglycemia, a correctable cause of seizures and altered mental status. Every seriously poisoned patient needs at least an initial ECG: a wide QRS points to a sodium channel blocker, a long QT to the risk of torsades. A routine urine drug screen is of questionable benefit, and most screens miss fentanyl, ketamine and GHB. Charcoal waits until the airway is judged safe, and flumazenil is not a nonspecific coma-reversal drug.

nodes.summary: Cardiac arrest or unexplained shock after an overdose: standard resuscitation and the poison center (1-800-222-1222); poisoning-specific arrest care is not in this version.

Seizing after an overdose: airway, oxygen and a glucose, then a benzodiazepine first. Continue in the seizure pathway (pw_seizure) for benzodiazepine doses and its isoniazid route (pyridoxine). In a toxin-induced seizure that outlasts the benzodiazepine, a barbiturate may be the second-line agent; phenytoin is generally not recommended in the severely poisoned. Then the ECG for a wide QRS, acetaminophen and salicylate levels for an intentional ingestion, and a psychiatric assessment.

Octreotide is listed with glucose as an antidote for sulfonylureas, but no open source read gives its dose, and the dextrose is not delayed for it.

nodes.why: For a known or suspected opioid overdose the label gives 0.4 to 2 mg IV, repeated at 2 to 3 minute intervals until breathing improves, IM or subcutaneously if there is no IV route. If 10 mg brings no response, the diagnosis should be questioned, so 10 mg is a ceiling for doubt, not a starting push. In someone physically dependent on opioids an abrupt, complete reversal precipitates withdrawal; small increments may reduce that risk. Flumazenil is not a nonspecific coma-reversal drug.

nodes.ask: QRS 0.10 seconds or more after an overdose. Next?
options: IV sodium bicarbonate, serum pH 7.45 to 7.55
IV procainamide for the wide-complex tachycardia
Physostigmine for the dry skin and dilated pupils
Flumazenil 0.2 mg IV for the drowsiness
nodes.chainStep: IV sodium bicarbonate to keep the serum pH at 7.45 to 7.55 (avoid a pH over 7.60); cardiac monitoring; early intubation for CNS depression; benzodiazepines for seizures
nodes.why: In tricyclic overdose a limb-lead QRS of 0.10 seconds or more may be the best indication of severity, and IV sodium bicarbonate holds the serum pH at 7.45 to 7.55; hyperventilation can be added with extreme caution, but a pH over 7.60 or a PCO2 under 20 is undesirable. Class 1A and 1C antiarrhythmics such as procainamide are generally contraindicated. Physostigmine is not recommended except for life-threatening symptoms unresponsive to other therapy, and flumazenil is contraindicated with signs of serious cyclic antidepressant overdose.

nodes.summary: Tricyclic or other sodium channel blocker overdose with a wide QRS: IV sodium bicarbonate to a serum pH of 7.45 to 7.55, cardiac monitoring for at least 6 hours and longer while any toxicity persists, early intubation for CNS depression and benzodiazepines for seizures; no class 1A or 1C antiarrhythmics, no flumazenil, no physostigmine. Because the overdose is often deliberate, a psychiatric assessment follows. An intentional ingestion also needs acetaminophen and salicylate levels.

Ventricular dysrhythmia despite sodium bicarbonate (and cautious hyperventilation): the label lists lidocaine among the drugs that may help, with class 1A and 1C antiarrhythmics contraindicated; hemoperfusion is rarely beneficial for refractory instability, and hemodialysis is ineffective. Doses are not in the open sources read: call the poison center. Psychiatric assessment once stable. An intentional ingestion also needs acetaminophen and salicylate levels.

nodes.why: Physostigmine reverses the central effects of drugs that cause the anticholinergic syndrome: the US label gives 2 mg IM or slowly IV, no faster than 1 mg a minute, repeated if life-threatening signs such as arrhythmia, convulsions or coma recur. results.front: Talking in full sentences, airway safe; glucose 102 mg/dL. ECG: sinus tachycardia 132, QRS 92 ms, no ST elevation.
results.tox_exam: Pupils dilated; skin drenched in sweat; normal tone, no clonus; bowel sounds present.

cases.label: Jimsonweed, anticholinergic
cases.vignette: 19-year-old man brought by friends after drinking a tea brewed from seeds at a party; he is picking at the air and mumbling. HR 126, BP 148/90, RR 18, temperature 38.4 C, SpO2 98%. Healthy, no medical history.

results.front: Airway safe; glucose 110 mg/dL. ECG: sinus tachycardia 126, QRS 88 ms.
results.tox_exam: Pupils dilated and sluggish; skin hot, flushed and dry; dry mouth; bowel sounds absent; bladder palpable. A friend says the seeds were jimsonweed.

cases.label: Serotonin toxicity
cases.vignette: 55-year-old woman on sertraline who started tramadol for back pain 2 days ago; now agitated, shaking and sweating. HR 118, BP 158/92, RR 20, temperature 38.6 C.

results.front: Airway safe; glucose 120 mg/dL. ECG: sinus tachycardia 118, QRS 90 ms.
results.tox_exam: Pupils dilated; sweating; hyperactive bowel sounds; brisk reflexes with sustained ankle clonus.

cases.label: Acetaminophen above the treatment line
cases.vignette: 22-year-old woman who says she swallowed 40 extra-strength acetaminophen tablets 40 minutes ago, after a breakup; she feels well. HR 96, BP 118/74, RR 16, SpO2 99%. Weight 60 kg.

results.front: Airway safe; glucose 96 mg/dL. ECG: sinus rhythm 96, QRS 84 ms, QTc 420 ms.
results.tox_exam: Pupils, skin, tone and reflexes normal.
results.decon_time: Forty minutes since one ingestion of 500 mg acetaminophen tablets; alert, protecting her airway, not vomiting.
results.levels_result: 4 hours after the ingestion: acetaminophen 180 mcg/mL; salicylate undetectable; ALT 22 U/L; chemistry normal.
results.apap_line: 180 mcg/mL at 4 hours lies above the treatment line.
results.nac_after: After the last bag: acetaminophen undetectable, ALT 30 U/L, INR 1.0.

cases.label: Acetaminophen below the treatment line
cases.vignette: 31-year-old man who took a handful of acetaminophen tablets at 9 pm after losing his job and came in at 2 am, worried. He rarely drinks, eats normally and takes no medicines. HR 84, BP 124/78, SpO2 99%.

results.front: Airway safe; glucose 101 mg/dL. ECG: sinus rhythm 84, QRS 86 ms.
results.decon_time: Five hours since one ingestion at a known time.
results.levels_result: 5 hours after the ingestion: acetaminophen 60 mcg/mL; salicylate undetectable; ALT 25 U/L; chemistry normal.
results.apap_line: 60 mcg/mL at 5 hours lies below the treatment line.

cases.label: Acetaminophen, time unknown
cases.vignette: 44-year-old woman found by her sister, nauseated and tired, beside empty acetaminophen bottles and a note; she cannot say when she took them. HR 102, BP 112/70, RR 18, SpO2 98%. Weight 70 kg.

results.front: Airway safe; glucose 88 mg/dL. ECG: sinus tachycardia 102, QRS 86 ms.
results.decon_time: Time of ingestion unknown, probably spread over many hours.
results.levels_result: Acetaminophen 38 mcg/mL; ALT 410 U/L; INR 1.4; salicylate undetectable; chemistry otherwise normal.
results.nac_after: After the last bag: acetaminophen 8 mcg/mL, ALT 1,250 U/L, INR 1.9.

cases.label: Salicylate toxicity, alkalinization works
cases.vignette: 39-year-old man who took most of a bottle of 325 mg aspirin tablets 3 hours ago, meaning to harm himself; ringing in his ears and vomiting. HR 108, BP 128/80, RR 28 and deep, SpO2 98%. Weight 80 kg.

results.front: Alert, airway safe; glucose 132 mg/dL. ECG: sinus tachycardia 108, QRS 90 ms.
results.tox_exam: Pupils normal; normal tone, no clonus; no toxidrome pattern.
results.decon_time: Three hours since the ingestion; vomiting.
results.levels_result: Salicylate 58 mg/dL; pH 7.42, PCO2 26, bicarbonate 16, anion gap 22; potassium 3.4 mEq/L; acetaminophen undetectable.
results.sal_resp: Six hours later: salicylate 38 mg/dL and falling, urine pH 7.8, potassium 4.0 mEq/L, alert.

cases.label: Salicylate toxicity, dialysis
cases.vignette: 67-year-old woman with chronic kidney disease (creatinine 1.8 mg/dL) who tells EMS she swallowed two bottles of aspirin 45 minutes ago to end her life; nausea and ringing in her ears. HR 112, BP 136/82, RR 26, SpO2 97%.

results.front: Alert and oriented, airway safe; glucose 140 mg/dL. ECG: sinus tachycardia 112, QRS 92 ms.
results.decon_time: Forty-five minutes since the ingestion of plain aspirin; alert, airway safe, not vomiting.
results.levels_result: Salicylate 72 mg/dL at 2 hours; pH 7.38, PCO2 24, bicarbonate 14, anion gap 24; acetaminophen undetectable.
results.sal_resp: Four hours later on bicarbonate: salicylate 96 mg/dL and rising; she is now confused and needs oxygen for a falling saturation.

cases.label: Ethylene glycol, dialysis
cases.vignette: 50-year-old man brought in vomiting and drowsy after drinking from a bottle in his garage hours ago; his wife says it was on purpose. HR 112, BP 132/84, RR 30, SpO2 97%.

results.front: Drowsy but rousable, airway safe; glucose 104 mg/dL. ECG: sinus tachycardia 112, QRS 92 ms.
results.tox_exam: Pupils normal; deep, fast breathing; no toxidrome pattern.
results.decon_time: Several hours since the ingestion; the bottle is antifreeze.
results.levels_result: pH 7.12, bicarbonate 6, anion gap 31, osmolal gap 38; creatinine 2.4 mg/dL (0.9 last year); calcium oxalate crystals in the urine; acetaminophen and salicylate undetectable.
results.alc_result: Six hours later: creatinine 3.1 mg/dL, urine output falling, anion gap still 30.

cases.label: Methanol, fomepizole alone
cases.vignette: 35-year-old woman who drank windshield washer fluid 3 hours ago after an argument and called 911 herself. HR 94, BP 122/76, RR 18, SpO2 99%.

results.front: Alert, airway safe; glucose 98 mg/dL. ECG: sinus rhythm 94, QRS 86 ms.
results.tox_exam: Pupils normal, vision normal; no toxidrome pattern.
results.decon_time: Three hours since she drank the washer fluid.
results.levels_result: pH 7.33, bicarbonate 19, anion gap 19, osmolal gap 20; creatinine 0.8 mg/dL; acetaminophen and salicylate undetectable.
results.alc_result: Methanol level 34 mg/dL; on fomepizole pH 7.35, creatinine 0.8 mg/dL, vision normal.

cases.label: Lithium overdose, dialysis
cases.vignette: 46-year-old man with bipolar disorder who took a week of his lithium tablets at once last night, wanting to die; now confused, tremulous and unsteady. HR 92, BP 118/72, RR 16, SpO2 98%.

results.front: Confused but answering, airway safe; glucose 106 mg/dL. ECG: sinus rhythm 92, QRS 92 ms.
results.tox_exam: Coarse tremor and ataxia; pupils normal; no sweating, no clonus.
results.decon_time: About 14 hours since the ingestion of immediate-release tablets.
results.levels_result: Lithium 4.6 mEq/L; sodium 141 mEq/L; creatinine 1.5 mg/dL; acetaminophen and salicylate undetectable.

cases.label: Iron overdose in shock
cases.vignette: 26-year-old woman who swallowed a bottle of her ferrous sulfate tablets 2 hours ago after an argument, to hurt herself; vomiting. HR 104, BP 112/70, RR 18, SpO2 99%.

results.front: Airway safe; glucose 112 mg/dL. ECG: sinus tachycardia 104, QRS 88 ms. Pregnancy test negative.
results.tox_exam: Pupils normal; abdominal tenderness; no toxidrome pattern.
results.decon_time: Two hours since the ingestion of ferrous sulfate tablets; pressure normal, bowel sounds present, airway safe.
results.levels_result: Now vomiting blood-streaked fluid; BP 82/50, HR 128; pH 7.21, lactate 6 mmol/L; serum iron markedly raised; acetaminophen and salicylate undetectable.

cases.label: Cardiac arrest after an overdose
cases.vignette: 52-year-old woman found unresponsive at home beside empty pill bottles; EMS started CPR on the way in.

results.front: No pulse; the monitor shows pulseless electrical activity. Fingerstick glucose 98 mg/dL.

cases.label: Coma, naloxone fails, no drug found
cases.vignette: 63-year-old man found unresponsive in his apartment by a neighbor; no pill bottles, syringes or notes. RR 7, SpO2 86% on air, HR 70, BP 172/98.

results.front: Pupils small but reactive; lungs clear and dry; glucose 128 mg/dL. ECG: sinus rhythm, QRS 90 ms.
results.nalox_resp: No change after naloxone, 10 mg in total; a search of the apartment finds no drugs.

cases.label: Lithium overdose, moderate
cases.vignette: 38-year-old woman with bipolar disorder who took 20 of her sustained-release lithium tablets 3 hours ago after an argument, to hurt herself; nauseated, with a fine tremor. HR 88, BP 124/76, RR 16, SpO2 99%.

results.front: Alert and oriented, airway safe; glucose 104 mg/dL. ECG: sinus rhythm 88, QRS 90 ms.
results.tox_exam: Fine tremor; pupils normal; no sweating, no clonus.
results.decon_time: Three hours since the ingestion of sustained-release lithium; alert, pressure normal, bowel sounds present.
results.levels_result: Lithium 2.6 mEq/L; alert and oriented; sodium 139 mEq/L; creatinine 0.9 mg/dL; acetaminophen and salicylate undetectable.

cases.label: Acetaminophen below the line, with risk factors
cases.vignette: 45-year-old man who drinks most of a bottle of vodka every day took a handful of acetaminophen tablets 30 minutes ago after a fight, saying he wanted to die; he is drunk and drowsy, rousable to voice. HR 98, BP 132/80, RR 14, SpO2 96%. Weight 82 kg.

results.front: Rousable, maintaining his airway; glucose 92 mg/dL. ECG: sinus rhythm 98, QRS 88 ms.
results.tox_exam: Pupils normal; smells of alcohol; no toxidrome pattern.
results.decon_time: Thirty minutes since one ingestion of acetaminophen tablets; drowsy from alcohol, not fully conscious.
results.levels_result: 4 hours after the ingestion: acetaminophen 110 mcg/mL; salicylate undetectable; ALT 48 U/L; chemistry otherwise normal.
results.apap_line: 110 mcg/mL at 4 hours lies below the treatment line; he drinks heavily every day.
results.nac_after: After the last bag: acetaminophen undetectable, ALT 50 U/L and not rising, INR 1.1.
